source.title: Same Concept, Different Directions: Cross-Modal Feature Heterogeneity in Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Chung-Pa Lee; Jihoon Kwon; Kyle Min; Jy-yong Sohn

record.file_problem: The full paper is present; some equations and figure content are flattened in the web text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies cross-modal directions of SAE features and latent alignment in vision-language embeddings, not polysemanticity of individual neurons or the behavior described by the claim versions. Its feature-geometry results are related but do not test those versions.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses polysemantic embeddings and measures cross-modal feature heterogeneity, but its units of analysis are SAE decoder features and latent coordinates, not individual neurons responding to unrelated inputs. Related feature-geometry results are recorded with versions ["none"]. Downstream method comparisons and monosemanticity-score comparisons do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper studies whether image and text SAE features for the same concept share directions in VLM joint embeddings, and proposes modality-specific SAEs with post-hoc alignment. It assumes embeddings are polysemantic (a linear combination of features) but never measures individual neurons responding to unrelated inputs. It does not vary architecture to change neuron polysemanticity, and does not test superposition as a cause of neuron polysemanticity. Theorem 1 on limited SAE capacity concerns SAE latents, not trained-network neurons.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors also show, through Propositions 1 and 2 and the synthetic experiments, that auxiliary alignment losses trade reconstruction quality for latent alignment. They report that their post-hoc alignment improves retrieval and steering while matching the reconstruction error of modality-specific SAEs.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies cross-modal SAE feature geometry and proposes modality-specific SAEs with post-hoc alignment; it does not reproduce the original neuron-analysis method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported feature-direction distance distributions vary with coactivation correlation and are examined across VLM families and model sizes. The paper also varies synthetic cross-modal feature distance and SAE capacity.

fits_no_version.finding: In four base-size and four large-size VLMs, image and text SAE feature pairs that coactivate strongly still have direction distances that do not concentrate near zero. Two CLIP examples have distances of 0.42 and 0.50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Semantically corresponding image and text SAE features in CLIP-like joint embeddings need not share a direction.

fits_no_version.finding: When an SAE has fewer latents than image and text feature directions (m < 2n), distinct directions must share a coordinate, leaving positive reconstruction loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Limited SAE latent capacity collapses distinct cross-modal feature directions into shared latents.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, 2026; peer-review status not stated
record.problems: The authors state that the analysis relies on the linear representation hypothesis and simplified generative assumptions. Feature correspondence is inferred from coactivation as a proxy, and the paper notes this may be less accurate in noisy or weakly aligned settings. The web-extracted figures do not provide exact distribution values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No results testing the claim versions were reported. Downstream retrieval, classification, concept-steering, and method-comparison results were not recorded because they evaluate the proposed SAE method rather than individual-neuron polysemanticity.

untested.parts: Neurons in image classifiers responding to unrelated inputs.
Share of MLP neurons in language models responding to unrelated tokens, and how it varies by layer.
Superposition as the cause of polysemanticity in trained-network neurons.
How the share of polysemantic neurons changes with activation function, architecture or regularization.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons are misread instances of one shared feature.
Whether neuron polysemanticity depends on the activation range examined or the explanation-scoring method.

record.verdict_notes: The paper uses 'polysemantic' only for whole embedding vectors. Figure 8's monosemanticity scores compare the authors' SAE method with baselines, so they are not a test of neuron polysemanticity. The record's reading as T6/discusses is upheld.

versions.untested_parts: Individual neurons in image classifiers responding to multiple unrelated image inputs.
MLP neurons in transformer language models and their responses to tokens or contexts.
Whether polysemanticity of trained-network neurons is caused by representing more sparse features than neurons. The paper analyzes SAE latent capacity, not neuron polysemanticity.
Polysemantic neurons arising without capacity pressure from initialization, regularization, or training noise.
Changes in the share of polysemantic neurons across architectures, activation functions, or regularization, and associated performance costs.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons detect a shared feature or related jobs rather than unrelated mixtures.
Whether neuron polysemanticity depends on activation range examined or explanation-scoring method.

rows.operation_detail: Theoretical analysis of reconstruction minimization under limited SAE latent capacity.

conditions.value: Fewer latent coordinates than total image and text feature directions

rows.measure: Reconstruction loss when distinct feature directions are assigned to SAE decoder columns
rows.value: At least two distinct directions must share a coordinate; the minimum reconstruction loss is strictly positive for s sufficiently close to 1
rows.note: This is a theoretical result about SAE latent capacity and feature directions, not a measurement of polysemantic neurons in trained networks.
rows.check: Theoretical result about SAE latent capacity forcing distinct feature directions to share a coordinate. It is superposition-like in the SAE, but it says nothing about why trained-network neurons are polysemantic. It is a proof, not a measurement.

relation.reason: It only says VLM embeddings are polysemantic, as a premise about whole embedding vectors (Section 3), not neurons. It measures SAE features. 'discusses' is acceptable.

tranche.reason: The paper studies cross-modal direction mismatch of SAE features in VLM embeddings. It measures no network neurons and has no result on any version of the polysemantic-neuron claim.

source_check.notes: No row bears on a version: all are about SAE feature directions (Figures 2, 3, 9) or SAE capacity (Theorem 1), not neurons of the trained network. 'Polysemantic' appears only as an explicit premise about embedding vectors, so 'assumes' would also be defensible for the relation. SigLIP2 is labelled 'SigLIP Base' and 'SigLIP Large' in the figures.
